about: Traceability of the 33 specified requirements to what Chemifree implements now. Statuses describe this product only; nothing here claims chemistry, file formats, or equivalence with another program.
status_rule: A requirement's status is derived from its parts: intentionally_rejected when every part is; implemented when every part is implemented or intentionally_rejected; otherwise partial when any part is implemented or partial; otherwise unverified when any part is; otherwise not_implemented.

requirements.summary: Keep the chemical graph, its drawn scene instances, containment, and external references in separate namespaces.

parts.summary: Documents, atoms, and bonds have stable identifiers that are never reused, and bonds may only reference existing atoms; files with dangling or duplicate references are refused.
Not covered yet: Separate graph, scene instances, pages, containment, and external references; the document keeps one position per atom.

requirements.summary: Represent elements, isotopes, charges, hydrogen states, radicals, and query atoms and bonds.

parts.summary: Atoms record element (H to Og), formal charge (-8..8), and isotope mass number (1..999 or natural) as drawn; values outside those ranges are refused, and every field survives save and reopen. Nothing is computed from them.
Not covered yet: Hydrogen states, radicals, query atoms and bonds, aromatic and other bond types, valence, and their diagnostics.

requirements.summary: Define what a selection covers and which objects an edit affects, including nested containment.

parts.summary: Deleting atoms removes exactly their incident bonds, moving lists each atom once, and selection stays client state outside history.
Not covered yet: Groups, nested containment, multi-object transforms, clipboard, and scene-level selection scope.

requirements.summary: Apply edits atomically with consistent references, undo/redo, and revisions.

parts.summary: A transaction applies all of its commands or none; a refusal names the failing command index and allocates no identifiers.
Each effective change adds a revision, a change that leaves the drawing identical adds none, and a stale expected revision is refused with the current one.
Undo and redo restore exact earlier states as new revisions, a new edit drops the redo branch, and identifiers of undone objects are not reused.
Saving commits atomically; after a restart the saved drawing and its history reopen, unsaved edits without a draft are gone, and a recovery draft can be recovered.
Not covered yet: Transactions over scene objects, groups, stereo and templates, cross-document moves, and cancellable jobs.

requirements.summary: Version typed requests, state compatibility explicitly, and return structured errors.

parts.summary: HTTP and the CLI share one Application and one v1 JSON contract; every reply carries api_version and errors use one envelope with code, current_revision, command_index, and reason.
A repeated request_id with the same request returns the original reply without applying it again; reuse for a different request is refused.
The capability report lists chemistry, formats, model loading, authentication, and Windows integration as not implemented.
Not covered yet: Per-operation versioned contracts, compatibility profiles, cancellation and job errors, and the other entry points (MCP, scripting, packaged server).

requirements.summary: Check the product against a deterministic, independently written conformance corpus.

parts.summary: A versioned conformance runner drives the shared Application on fresh data directories, counts accept and reject cases apart, and reports pending cases as not run with their follow-up.
The drawing slice has repeatable checks: Rust tests, the HTTP/CLI contract smoke, and the browser smoke in CI.
Not covered yet: Differential comparison on separate graph, stereo, numeric, scene, encoding, and host axes against an independent corpus.

requirements.summary: Keep analysis and implementation contexts and their artifacts apart.

parts.summary: Tracked files are checked for local-only paths, executables and native libraries, files over 1 MiB, the specified program's names, and byte copies of specification files. Reworded or re-encoded private data is not detected.
Specification inputs are referenced by path and SHA-256, and only derived IDs, counts, and own-words summaries are recorded.
Not covered yet: Input allowlists for the implementation context and the DATA reader's manifest, context, hash, and format checks.
